raw_segments.text: Cassius, therefore, good Brutus, be prepared to hear, and since you know you cannot see
yourself so well as by reflection, I, your glass, will modestly discover to yourself
that of yourself which you yet know not of.
And be not jealous on me, gentle Brutus.
Were I a common laugher, or did use to stale with ordinary oaths my love to every new protestor?
If you know that I do fawn on men, and hug them hard, and after scandal them, or if you
know that I profess myself in banqueting to all the rout, then hold me dangerous.
